craft_notes: Sthāyin: the defense — bheda-vāda cannot cancel authority. Sanskrit-first: 'pi twice kept (even-in-bheda, even-in-one-Lord's-work); akiṃcitkara kept powerless as the last adjective. Rows: 9 (undenied/unstopped pair), 1 ('powerless' closes — the negation lands on contradiction itself). Close: 'mutual contradiction from subject-difference powerless.' Rejected: 'irrelevant' — killed: akiṃcitkara is powerless (no force, not off-topic); resolving which side wins — killed: the point is bādha's emptiness, not victory.

lines: being one Lord's work — authority stands for now:
l4.sanskrit_cite: bhedavāde 'pi samastāgamānām ekeśvarakāryatve 'pi prāmāṇyaṃ tāvat avasthitam prāmāṇyanibandhanasya ekadeśasaṃvādasya avigītatāyā anidaṃtāpravṛtteś ca tulyatvāt parasparabādho viṣayabhedāt akiṃcitkaraḥ

reads_against.argmap: Does difference-doctrine cancel scripture's authority? → Even rival doctrines leave āgama's authority standing: contradiction by subject-difference alone is powerless.
c1_essence: Even in bheda-vāda the authority stands: mutual contradiction from subject-difference alone is powerless.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta-śānta of authority established (wonder settling into doctrinal calm)
